spots.label: Under the kitchen table
spots.text: Mum and Dad, voices low. Mum: 'That's the fourth this year. Heart failure. Again.' Dad: 'They were old.' 'Not that old. Not Mr. Okoro.' A pause. 'The lungs, Dan. I can't write down what's in the lungs.'

spots.label: The school office air vent
spots.text: The principal: 'We need a lamp-bearer by Tuesday.' Ms. Calloway: 'You'll have one.' 'The Calloway unit isn't in the guidance.' 'Neither is the mural.' Then, quietly: 'Sixty-three layers of paint.'

spots.label: Town Hall window ledge
spots.text: Delphine, to Hank, through a door: 'Nothing to report, Hank.' 'Good.' 'No. I mean it. I used to mean it. I have something to report.' Hank: 'Del. Don't.' The old clock, behind you, takes its minute.

spots.label: The clock shop door
spots.text: Silas, to a clock: 'Thaddeus, you would hate this. They put a child in a clean smock and ask him to carry a lamp to a place we both know.' He stops. 'I know you're there, young man. Come in and be bored.'

spots.label: The end of the dock
spots.text: You wave. The ripples wave back, in step. A voice, from nowhere you can point to: 'Hi, Tobi. Don't carry it. It's not fair. It only works because we're holding on.' You ask who 'we' is. 'All of us.' You ask how many. 'Lots. Too many. I counted.'

spots.label: Roy's hedge
spots.text: Roy on the swing, murmuring: 'Come in out of the wet, Amos. Come in, son.' The words are very quiet and very old.
